* fix(smoke): give teardown a real budget and name the survivors by @FerroxLabs in https://github.com/FerroxLabs/wayland/pull/1419
* fix(smoke): make a CDP timeout say which silence it is by @FerroxLabs in https://github.com/FerroxLabs/wayland/pull/1420

name: v0.11.9
body:
## Wayland 0.11.9 — your agent runs on your consent

This is a security-hardening release. The bundled engine moves to **wayland-core v0.12.19** (the GHSA-8r7g-7556-hj3j batch) and the whole approval path was rebuilt around one rule: nothing acts without your say-so. Below is what we actually changed and why, not just the headline.

---

### 🔒 Security hardening

**1. Auto-approving modes are opt-in at launch (wire-Force gate)**
- *The seam:* the agent accepts a `set_mode` instruction over its wire protocol. Nothing stopped a wire peer (a paired device, a programmatic client) from switching the agent into Force / AutoEdit / Autopilot — the modes that act without stopping to ask.
- *What we changed:* auto-approving modes now require an explicit local-operator opt-in taken **at boot** (`--force` or `WAYLAND_ALLOW_WIRE_FORCE=1`). `set_mode_from_wire` gates Force and AutoEdit behind that flag; with the gate closed (the default) the engine refuses a wire mode change outright. The model itself never emits `set_mode`, so a model can't induce it either.
- *Desktop side (#495):* the desktop opts the bundled engine into the gate so Autopilot keeps working for you, and in the same change we closed the remote-cron path — a paired-device WebSocket can no longer reach the cron write/exec/skill commands (`add-job`, `update-job`, `run-now`, `save-skill`, `confirm-proposal`). Local cron creation and read-only views are unaffected.

**2. Approvals are bound to the action**
- *The seam:* the approval token was effectively the tool-call id the model already knows, so an approval could in principle be correlated or replayed onto a different call.
- *What we changed:* approvals now carry a server-generated secret (`apr-<uuid>`) bound to the exact tool call. Resolving an approval over the wire requires that secret, not the model-visible id, so a "yes" to one action can't be reused for another.

**3. Project config can only tighten your posture, never loosen it**
- *The seam:* project-scoped configuration could widen the security posture (relax what the agent may do) when you opened a folder.
- *What we changed:* project config is now clamp-only. It can tighten the rules; directives that would loosen them are ignored. And project-config hooks are **default-deny** — a repo you open can't auto-run hooks without your explicit trust.

**4. Consistent MCP tool-name handling across every provider**
- *The seam:* tool names with certain characters or lengths were sanitized for OpenAI but passed verbatim to other providers, causing provider-specific 400 rejections.
- *What we changed:* a single shared codec (sentinel + hex-escape, with a 64-char clamp + hash for overlong names) is now applied uniformly across OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Cohere.

### 🧪 How this was verified (the part we don't usually show)
Every fix in this batch got an **independent adversarial cross-audit** by a reviewer that didn't write it, before merge. That process earned its keep here: on the cron work, the first audit found the initial remote-deny list was **incomplete** — two more remote-reachable commands (`save-skill`, `confirm-proposal`) could still reach the escalation path. We closed the entire command class and re-audited before it shipped. The final build was then live-verified as a signed, packaged app (cold boot smoke + an end-to-end voice capture test), not just green unit tests.

---

### ✨ Everyday improvements

**Project chats save to the project workspace (#494)**
- *The problem:* a chat created inside a project wrote its files to a per-chat Temporary Space instead of the project's shared folder, and that folder couldn't be opened from the UI.
- *What we changed:* conversations opened inside a project are re-homed to the project's shared workspace, so every chat in a project sees the same folder and it opens on click. The re-home is status-gated so an in-flight streaming turn is never killed mid-response when a conversation is reassigned.

**Voice dictation on the signed macOS build (#496)**
- *The problem:* dictation worked in a dev build but not in the signed/hardened macOS app, and speech-to-text expected its own separate key.
- *What we changed:* added the `com.apple.security.device.audio-input` entitlement and the `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` usage string to the signed build, and we request mic access **on demand** (when you first hit the mic) rather than at launch. Speech-to-text now reuses the key from a provider you've already connected (OpenAI Whisper), and bundled local Whisper (whisper-tiny) is the always-available offline floor when no cloud key is set.

---

### 🔧 Under the hood
- Bundled **wayland-core v0.12.16 → v0.12.19**.
- Google Workspace MCP updated **1.4.2 → 1.22.0** (it was crashing on import from a pydantic incompatibility). (#474)

### Install / update
Wayland **auto-updates** — open it and it's already pulling 0.11.9. Fresh install of the self-host CLI: `npm install -g getwayland`.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/FerroxLabs/wayland/compare/v0.11.8...v0.11.9

name: v0.11.4
body:
## Stop picking the best AI. Command all of them.

The real unlock was never choosing the best model. It's never having to choose one at all.

Wayland 0.11.4 runs every major AI side by side and fields the right one for the job automatically. And it now ships on a new engine, **Wayland Core 0.12.14 with Crucible**, our Mixture-of-Providers council, so the hardest problems can be worked by a whole panel of providers at once instead of a single model.

### ✨ Highlights

- **Mixture-of-Providers, powered by Crucible.** The bundled engine now packs Crucible, a cross-provider council that can convene multiple models on one task, let each take a swing, and fuse the strongest answer. In-app, **Flux Auto** routes each request to the best model automatically, so you stop guessing which AI to use.
- **Greatly improved chat streaming.** Hit send and watch it work: an inline orbit indicator that animates while the assistant runs and settles when it's done, a unified plain-English activity timeline across every backend, live reasoning summaries in the thinking block, smooth fast streaming, a per-message action toolbar the moment a turn completes, and a turn timer that stays accurate even when you switch chats.
- **Real tool-use on Windows, safely sandboxed.** Wayland runs real shell commands and tools on Windows inside a locked-down AppContainer sandbox, working on a clean non-developer machine, not just a developer's rig. Live-verified.
- **Your local models pull real weight.** Ollama and llama.cpp models run private and free, and now handle tools that used to break them, thanks to up-front capability detection with a graceful no-tools fallback.

### 🔧 Also in this release

- New engine **Wayland Core 0.12.14**: Crucible Mixture-of-Providers council, sharper cross-vendor cost and pricing accuracy, and the Windows AppContainer shell-tool fixes (grant-skip for missing dev caches, job-tree reap so commands return promptly).
- Accurate, live model catalogs for every connected provider; assistants run on Wayland Core by default; Grok "Sign in with X" stays authenticated via a single, race-free OAuth refresher.
- One-click assistants with starter-prompt grids, multi-model teams, and scheduled tasks.
- Cleaner billing-error classification, a hardened model picker that never strands you on an empty list, and a stack of reliability fixes across the app. 63 changes in this release.

Free to start. One click. No setup ceremony.

---

*Full technical notes: see [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/FerroxLabs/wayland/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).*

name: v0.11.3
body:
Wayland keeps getting stronger. 0.11.3 is about reach: connect any provider and it routes straight to where it belongs, a new first-class provider joins the lineup, your model catalogs stream live, and a stronger Wayland Core 0.12.8 engine runs underneath.

It auto-updates, so it's probably already pulling the new build.

## Models & providers

- **Connect any provider, it routes straight to its own endpoint.** Every connected key (Sakana, OpenRouter, and the whole OpenAI-compatible family) lands on the right provider, resolved through the v2 registry bridge at spawn.
- **Sakana AI (Fugu) joins as a first-class provider**, with its Fugu models and brand logo.
- **Live model catalogs** for ChatGPT subscription, MiniMax and DashScope, pulled straight from each provider so you always see the current lineup.
- **ChatGPT subscription** chats run through the engine's native ChatGPT provider and are selectable directly (#243).
- **Local Ollama models** appear in the picker and run keyless (#294, #268).
- **Claude Code starts on Opus** when no model is pinned, so you begin on the strongest model.
- **Smarter model guidance:** models without tool support point you to a tool-capable one instead of stalling a turn.

## Memory

- Your global **Wayland Memory** is wired into chat, so the assistant recalls you and your projects (#256).

## Experience & reliability

- Approval prompts are handled cleanly before a turn proceeds (#264).
- File preview is contained so it never interrupts the surrounding chat (#253).
- Smoother back-after-error navigation and Windows npm resolution (#254, #261).
- WSL-installed CLIs are detected on Windows (#258).
- MCP OAuth sign-in gains a timeout and a cancel (#242).
- Onboarding, workspace/history, and Doctor diagnostics sharpened (#249, #251, #274).
- Flux Voice speech-to-text gets its own config block with provider-scoped handling.
- More headroom for builds and typechecks (#260).

## Wayland Core engine

- Bundled engine updated to **v0.12.8**: adds the Sakana AI (Fugu) provider and carries the full hardening batch forward — stronger context-window sizing (#255), Windows reliability (#257, #262, #263, #267), image generation (#265), and ChatGPT sign-in import (#293).

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/FerroxLabs/wayland/compare/v0.11.2...v0.11.3
